newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae sets first global Hong Kong dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae sets first global Hong Kong dollar bond.

text.p: The HK$1.5 billion ($194 million) bond announced by Fannie Mae earlier on Wednesday is the first global issue the U.S. home loans group has launched in that currency.

"We have sold a lot of dollar-denominated securities to investors in Asia and the feedback was that they were also interested in a high-quality name issued in their own currency," Fannie Mae's debt marketing vice-president John The Losen said.
The five-year offering was priced to yield 61.6 basis points over the June 2002, 6.25 percent, U.S. Treasury note.
"We've seen institutional interest from China, Hong Kong and other Asian countries as well as some European countries and there's always the opportunity to reopen the issue," The Losen said.
Fannie Mae launched the first Australian and New Zealand dollar global bonds as well as the first global bond in sterling this year.
It also has dollar, mark and yen bonds in the global format, which allows the deal to be sold across the world and is not subject to sales restrictions that are imposed on Eurobonds.
In March Fannie Mae treasurer Linda Knight said the group was considering a global bond in lira, with plans for a French franc global on hold.
"We are always looking for funding opportunities in various currrencies and various markets," The Losen said, adding China's take-over of Hong Kong was seen as no risk to the currency.
Fannie Mae is rated triple-A by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp. In April the World Bank issued a HK$1.0 billion fixed-rate 10-year bond.
